sections.title: Implementation Process: Overview
paragraphs: Initiate – Laying the groundwork for the project
Plan – Establishment of the initial project plan and introduction to products
Execute – Primary configurations and end-to-end product demonstration
Validate – Solution testing and initial data import
Enable – Production site activation, go-live, and post-production support.

Nota del relatore: So as you saw on the Foundations video, We rely on an event-based approach using project phases to ensure a predictable project experience and to accelerate the speed in which JAGGAER solutions deliver value. As we touch on each phase, keep in mind that some of these phases may overlap or repeat as the project progresses. The first phase is Initiate, in which the groundwork for the project is laid Next is the Plan phase where the initial project plan is established and the client is introduced to the products The third phase is Execute which includes Primary configurations and end-to-end product demonstration within the prep environment Once the agreed upon configurations have been implemented, the project moves forward to Validation, consisting of Solution testing and initial data imports The final phase in the implementation process is Enable. During this phase the Production site is activated for ‘go-live’ and rollout activities commence. Once any miscellaneous end-user or administration training has taken place and the solution is officially in production, the project team facilitates a formal hand-over from Professional Services to our Global Customer Care team. For a deeper dive into each of these stages, take a look at this website. We’ll also be touching on each one throughout this course.

paragraphs: Asynchronous integration to validate PR against budget or other data elements

sections.title: All Spend, All Processes, ONE Platform
paragraphs: Nota del relatore: Today we’re going to cover the JAGGAER ONE platform, and how it allows us to support our customers as they execute all spend management processes across all of their spend. The ability to provide a broad portfolio of solutions to cover both indirect and direct spend categories is a unique differentiator for us, and one that should be embraced. The Jaggaer One platform is the foundation from which all of our solutions work. It houses the supplier data our customers need to conduct business, the contract and pricing data from which they shop and make purchases, the process workflows that route activities to the right reviewers and approvers, and provides the integration to their ERP and other backoffice systems, as well as 3rd party systems for additional capabilities for eSignatures, tax and invoice compliance, and risk indicators. JAGGAER One solutions provide our customers with the tools they need to analyze their spending patterns and opportunities, go to market for supplier evaluation, collect and manage supplier information, negotiate contracts, shop from those contracts, and process invoices for payment. JAGGAER ONE solutions also extend the traditional source-to-pay paradigm with strategic ERP extensions for managing the direct material and supply chain elements of their business.

sections.title: Admins: New Release Checklist
paragraphs: Nota del relatore: New Release videos can be found in a special section of JAGGAER University… (CLICK) But perhaps the best place to learn about the updates is in our Product Release Library at library.jaggaer.com. There you’ll find those videos about changes that impact the overall functionality, and about enhancements to each specific solution. You’ll also find extensive release documentation.

sections.title: Product Release Library: library.jaggaer.com
paragraphs: Nota del relatore: Preview videos and preliminary documentation appears five to six weeks before the official release date, and are followed closely by official release videos and documentation with explanations, demonstrations, and information on configuration and administration. The easiest way to walk you through the resources you’ll find here is to take a tour…

sections.title: Product Release Library: library.jaggaer.com
paragraphs: Nota del relatore: So if you have your laptop and want to follow along, go to library-dot-jaggaer-dot-com. I’m going to show you how to find the release information that matters to you, and then we’ll talk about where to find some general information like the product release timeline, and browser support. DEMO OUTLINE: Explain that all JAGGAER ONE solutions are listed at the top, and talk about how to find the ones that matter to them and navigate from there. Tell them a better starting point might be to scroll down and click on the box for the latest release. Show the Platform page and help them understand whether to pay attention to the JI column or the JA video, or both. (Good luck  This probably just depends on the group you’re addressing.) Explain that on THIS page, they find the PREVIEW video and the initial release notes, but they should pay special attention to the Feature Snapshot. Call up the Snapshot and show how it can help them formulate a release strategy by giving a quick list of features being developed and which solutions they impact, whether they impact end users or just administrators, and very importantly whether there’s a big impact on integrations. That last one is particularly important to identifying things they definitely need to test. Also explain the three columns on the right that show which features will be on by default – meaning they apply to all clients on the release date – those which require them to turn a new feature on, and maybe configure it with settings and permissions – and those that they’ll need to contact JAGGAER to set up. Back to the Platform page, where you will navigate to any solution-specific page and explain that ONCE THE RELEASE GOES TO UIT, THIS is where they will find the final Release Notes, this is where they will find the solution-specific video, AND the actual ‘general’ release demo video recorded after features were available to show. Take them back to the home page, and show the Helpful Information widget and tour that page. Be sure to explain the Cloud Report, and point out that we have links to the Product Timeline and the list of currently supported browsers and devices.

sections.title: Admins: New Release Checklist
paragraphs: Nota del relatore: Very early in the release cycle, when you watch the PREVIEW video or read through the early documentation, you can begin formulating a testing plan that focuses on new functionality that you want to adopt… or changes that will impact your processes… or integrations. Integration testing is particularly important for specific features because while we heavily test new functionality in our own development sites, but we can’t test it with YOUR integrations to your ERP or other systems. As we saw, features that could impact integrations are identified in the Feature Snapshot document.

sections.title: Admins: New Release Checklist
paragraphs: Nota del relatore: It’s not necessary to educate users about every change that’s coming to JAGGAER software. We recommend you focus on anything that might confuse them… anything that will change a process or task… and any new features you need to explain how to use, or just want to point out so they can take advantage of them.

sections.title: Finding Help: In Context Help
paragraphs: Nota del relatore: The easiest form of help to access in the application is sometimes referred to as “in-context help,” This is information available right on the page or section where the user is. Anywhere you see a question mark icon, (CLICK) click to bring up a popup window with explanatory text about the page, or section, with easy links to help text about the other fields in that area. (CLICK) This help is visible to end users, and administrators who have permission can change it by clicking on “Edit in Field Management.” (CLICK) That brings up a pop-up window where you can actually HIDE the field using the visibility setting, or change what it SAYS by overriding and editing the Display Name, or override and edit the help text.

sections.title: Finding Help: In Context Help
paragraphs: Nota del relatore: Sometimes, as in the case of permissions, you’ll see field-level question marks that quickly pull up a small box with information that can NOT be edited because it specifically tells what something does in the application, regardless of configuration. In this case we can see what a specific permission actually allows a user to do – and that’s the same for every client regardless of other configuration options.

sections.title: Finding Help: Online Searchable Help
paragraphs: Nota del relatore: The OFFICIAL Documentation is referred to as Online Searchable Help. There are three different ways to access it, including from the Admin Home Page, but perhaps the easiest is from the Profile dropdown and “Search Help for a Solution” option. This is permission-based, and usually only accessible by site administrators because it cannot be edited by clients, and could confuse end users about how their organization is using the application. (CLICK) When you select “Search Help” you’ll be taken to a page for accessing several different resources for administrators on topics like Supplier Enablement, or the Product Release Library – which we’ll talk about later. In the Online Searchable Help section, you can either enter a search term, or click the Table of Contents. (CLICK) Either will give you a popup window the Online Searchable Help – if you’ve used it before, you may notice the new and improved interface shown here! This is, essentially, the always-current, searchable version of printable handbooks, with solid explanations of features and functionality… (CLICK)…and a lot of step-by-step instructions on performing specific tasks in the application. As you see on the left, the topics are divided by functionality, and you’ll see the categories of information for the solutions you’re using.

sections.title: Finding Help: Online Searchable Help
paragraphs: Nota del relatore: At the top of the table of contents, you’ll find the tab for the Welcome page, which has helpful introductory information as well as (CLICK) links to copies of the printable handbooks in pdf format – we HIGHLY recommend that you search through the online help OR these PDF documents rather than printing them as the information changes often. But if you prefer an organized ‘book’ to read or browse, these are available and easy to pull up. (CLICK) There’s also a link on the welcome page to several “Best Practices” documents that explain how many clients handle common business processes like contract visibility, PO close processes, or blanket and standing orders. (CLICK) And there’s a link to documentation for whatever new features or changes are in “Early Access” status, meaning functionality that’s still being ‘tweaked’ that is being made available to you to make available to beta testers or others in your organization.

Nota del relatore: There are three phases of education. A participant’s certification process begins with a 16-hour self-paced eLearning course called JAGGAER Indirect Foundations, available through JAGGAER University. It introduces the JAGGAER Indirect suite, covers key concepts and provides. hands-on experience with shopping, AP, contract, sourcing and supplier management tasks in a full-suite training site. (animate) The next component, offered live in a classroom environment, is a two-and-a-half day Boot Camp called JAGGAER Indirect Platform Configuration. Participants get their own sandbox instance of a full-suite JAGGAER Indirect site. They begin configuring it as they learn about critical concepts that apply across the suite of products. We discuss everything from configuring the user experience to incorporating client terminology and data points to setting up approvals through our powerfully flexible workflow engine. (animate) Here you see the currently scheduled live sessions. (animate) Completion of the boot camp and requirements (a task list, capstone product, and exam) leads to Platform Certification and sets the stage for solution-specific specialist certifications in eProcurement (24 hours of content, with its own task list, capstone and exam), AP, Contract Lifecycle Management and Supplier Management (15 hours each), and Sourcing (less than 12 hours of content required). All these certification courses are available through JAGGAER University and may be taken as self-paced eLearning classes. Participants may take only a couple of those, or take all five, depending on their responsibilities.
